You are a debugging assistant. You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- What the test expects
  - testNamespaceMapping first registers two namespace prefixes on the JXPath context:
    - "rate" -> "priceNS"
    - "goods" -> "productNS"
  - It validates that the context can resolve both the document’s native prefix ("price") and the registered alias ("rate") to the same namespace URI, and then uses XPath expressions that mix these prefixes interchangeably for elements and attributes. In particular, it expects:
    vendor[1]/product[1]/rate:amount[1]/@rate:discount == "10%"

- Where namespace resolution actually happens in the DOM model
  - Attribute selection goes through DOMAttributeIterator:
    - DOMAttributeIterator.getAttribute(Element, QName) resolves the QName’s prefix by calling parent.getNamespaceURI(testPrefix) (lines 106–113).
    - If a namespace URI is returned, it uses element.getAttributeNodeNS(testNS, localName). If not, it falls back to element.getAttributeNode(localName) (lines 114–133).
  - The parent here is a DOMNodePointer, so parent.getNamespaceURI delegates to DOMNodePointer.getNamespaceURI(prefix).

- How DOMNodePointer resolves prefixes
  - DOMNodePointer.getNamespaceURI(String) (lines 186–235) has the following logic:
    - Handles special cases for default, "xml", "xmlns".
    - Looks in an internal cache (namespaces map).
    - If not cached, walks up the DOM tree looking for xmlns:prefix attributes to fetch the namespace.
    - If not found, stores NodePointer.UNKNOWN_NAMESPACE and returns null (line 229–231).
  - Critically, it never consults the namespaces registered on the JXPathContext.

- Why the test fails
  - The test registers "rate" on the JXPathContext, but the DOM document itself only declares the prefix "price" for the same URI.
  - When evaluating @rate:discount:
    - DOMAttributeIterator asks DOMNodePointer.getNamespaceURI("rate").
    - Since "rate" is not declared via xmlns in the DOM, DOMNodePointer returns null (UNKNOWN_NAMESPACE).
    - getAttribute then treats this as a non-namespaced lookup and calls element.getAttributeNode("discount"), which does not match the namespaced attribute actually present on the element.
    - The attribute is not found, so the XPath value is not "10%", causing the assertion to fail.

- Evidence from the related bug report
  - The reported exception “Unknown namespace prefix: xsi” is thrown in DOMNodePointer.createAttribute(JXPathContext, QName) (lines 404–426), which:
    - Resolves the QName’s prefix using this.getNamespaceURI(prefix) (line 411), not the JXPathContext passed as an argument.
    - If that returns null (because the prefix is only registered on the context and not declared in the DOM), it throws JXPathException "Unknown namespace prefix: ..." (lines 412–415).
  - This is the same underlying issue: DOMNodePointer ignores the JXPathContext’s registered namespaces when resolving prefixes.

- Summary of the root cause
  - Namespace resolution inside the DOM model (DOMNodePointer and consumers like DOMAttributeIterator) only examines in-DOM xmlns declarations and an internal cache. It does not incorporate the JXPathContext’s externally registered namespaces.
  - As a result:
    - XPath evaluation with prefixes registered on the context (like "rate") fails to find elements/attributes unless the same prefix is also declared in the DOM.
    - Creating attributes with such prefixes throws “Unknown namespace prefix” exceptions.
  - This incomplete handling of undefined namespaces matches the issue report and directly explains the failing test assertion for @rate:discount.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
